title.en: Terminal molecular random and total heat flux
title.zh: 终态分子随机与总热通量归约

summary: Reduce a terminal H2 distribution to random and total axial energy-flux profiles with a caller-supplied thermal speed, mass ratio and cylindrical velocity quadrature.

identity.relation: terminal H2 random and total axial heat-flux reduction
identity.direction: terminal (vr,vx,x) distribution, normalized velocity nodes, explicit mass and thermal speed, quadrature -> two x profiles
identity.definition: For each spatial cell k, density=sum_i weight[i]*sum_j f[i,j,k]*dvx[j] and particle_flux=Vth*sum_i weight[i]*sum_j vx[j]*f[i,j,k]*dvx[j], using the saved per-cell matrix-vector and radial order. Let u=particle_flux/density, c_x=vx-u/Vth, c_squared=vr^2+c_x^2, and m=2*mass_ratio*1.6726231e-27 kg. The random flux is 0.5*m*Vth^3 times the weighted integral of c_squared*c_x*f. Pressure is m*Vth^2/(3*1.602177e-19) times the weighted integral of c_squared*f, and axial stress is m*Vth^2/1.602177e-19 times the weighted integral of c_x^2*f minus pressure. Total flux is (0.5*density*m*u^2+2.5*pressure*1.602177e-19)*u+1.602177e-19*axial_stress*u+random_flux. On finite exact arithmetic it equals the raw kinetic-energy flux 0.5*m*Vth^3 times the weighted integral of (vr^2+vx^2)*vx*f.
identity.model: saved KN1DPy terminal H2 energy-moment diagnostic with caller-supplied mass ratio and thermal speed
identity.geometry: one-dimensional x profile over cylindrical (vr,vx) velocity cells
identity.coordinates: radial and axial velocity nodes are dimensionless speeds normalized by the supplied thermal speed; radial nodes are nonnegative and axial nodes may be signed
identity.boundary: finite nonnegative nonempty three-dimensional distribution; finite one-dimensional aligned velocity nodes and nonnegative quadrature weights; positive scalar mass ratio and thermal speed; positive integrated density in every x cell
assumptions: On positive quadrature weights the random-flux field agrees with scirel.kinetic.axisymmetric-neutral-moments when its derived thermal speed equals this caller-supplied speed and molecularity is 2. The total-flux field is additional; this terminal relation allows zero weights and does not expose the intermediate pressure or stress fields.
The mass ratio multiplies the saved hydrogen mass constant, not a standard atomic mass unit; the H2 mass uses twice that factor.

The callable neither establishes the upstream terminal distribution nor validates a full KN1D terminal closure. Boolean, complex and numeric-string coercions in the saved implementation are excluded by the maintained real-numeric contract.

inputs.name: radial_velocity_normalized
inputs.constraints: Finite, nonnegative, nonempty and one-dimensional; zero nodes are allowed and no monotonicity gate is imposed.

inputs.name: axial_velocity_normalized
inputs.constraints: Finite, nonempty and one-dimensional; zero nodes are allowed and no monotonicity gate is imposed.

inputs.name: mass_ratio
inputs.description: Positive factor of the saved hydrogen mass used for the H2 particle mass.
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; boolean and numeric-string coercions are rejected.

inputs.name: thermal_speed_m_s
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; no speed is derived from temperature in this callable.

inputs.name: terminal_distribution
inputs.description: Terminal H2 velocity distribution by spatial cell.
inputs.constraints: Finite, nonnegative and nonempty with exactly three axes.

inputs.name: cylindrical_weight
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative; zero cells are allowed if every integrated density remains positive.

inputs.name: dvx
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative; zero cells are allowed if every integrated density remains positive.

outputs.name: random_heat_flux_profile_w_m2
outputs.units: W/m^2 on the source distribution normalization
outputs.constraints: Finite and signed; follows the centered axial velocity.

outputs.name: total_heat_flux_profile_w_m2
outputs.description: Total axial kinetic-energy flux profile, including convective and random terms.
outputs.units: W/m^2 on the source distribution normalization
outputs.constraints: Finite and signed; follows the source's pressure/stress decomposition.

preconditions: The caller supplies a terminal H2 distribution aligned to the explicit cylindrical velocity quadrature.
Each spatial slice has strictly positive integrated density.
supported: Stateless terminal H2 random and total heat-flux reduction on finite cylindrical carriers, including some zero quadrature cells.
excluded: Terminal generation-state selection, energy-transfer rates, wall-source feedback and external physical validation.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for non-real numeric or non-finite inputs, malformed axes, negative radial nodes/distribution/weights/widths, nonpositive mass ratio or thermal speed, or nonpositive integrated density.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if a random or total heat-flux output becomes non-finite; no partial mapping is returned.

python.signature: reduce_terminal_molecular_heat_flux(radial_velocity_normalized, axial_velocity_normalized, mass_ratio, thermal_speed_m_s, terminal_distribution, cylindrical_weight, dvx)

example.description: Reduce one terminal H2 spatial cell with a zero axial node and a zero-width cell.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic import reduce_terminal_molecular_heat_flux
vr = np.array([0.5, 1.0])
vx = np.array([-1.0, 0.0, 2.0])
f = np.ones((2, 3, 1))
r = reduce_terminal_molecular_heat_flux(vr, vx, 1.0, 5000.0, f, np.array([1.0, 2.0]), np.array([0.5, 0.0, 0.25]))
assert set(r) == {'random_heat_flux_profile_w_m2', 'total_heat_flux_profile_w_m2'}
assert r['random_heat_flux_profile_w_m2'].shape == (1,)
assert all(np.isfinite(value).all() for value in r.values())
example.expected: Two finite one-cell heat-flux profiles; a zero axial node and a zero-width cell are accepted when integrated density remains positive.

scope: Independent per-cell centered and raw energy-flux integrals check both outputs on a nonuniform signed carrier.
Positive-weight random-flux overlap agrees with the existing nine-moment relation; zero-weight acceptance distinguishes their contracts.
Three SHA-gated historical cases cover exact finite replay and the saved boolean-coercion divergence.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Direct and optional saved comparisons establish the finite discrete heat-flux relation and boundary differences on tested carriers. They do not establish the upstream terminal distribution, physical normalization, whole-source D1 qualification or expert approval.
known_limitations: The source's strict D1 qualification is withdrawn; historical parity is only bounded development evidence.
The physical normalization of the supplied distribution requires expert review.
